Glossary for Confluence (Terms Definitio.review: Glossary for Confluence is a useful and easy-to-use app for organizing important terms directly in Confluence. Creating terms and adding details like synonyms, abbreviations, and labels was straightforward. Overall, it can make documentation easier to understand, especially for onboarding and internal processes.

The app was easy to use once the glossary was set up, and adding terms, definitions, synonyms and labels felt straightforward. The page highlighting and glossary macros were especially useful because definitions could be shown directly inside Confluence pages. I did face some confusion during the initial setup and glossary navigation, but overall the app worked well for organizing and reusing shared terminology.

Glossary for Confluence provides a useful set of features for managing shared terminology directly within Confluence. Creating and organizing terms was straightforward, and features such as synonyms, abbreviations, labels, attachments, term highlighting, CSV import, and multilingual translations were useful and generally easy to understand. The Term List macro and Glossary Highlight feature worked well and made glossary content accessible from Confluence pages. The multilingual workflow was also effective once enabled. However, I encountered several usability issues during testing. Floating support and feedback widgets sometimes covered important controls such as Save and Apply Filter. Some dropdowns and scrollbars were partially clipped, CSV import did not clearly report invalid rows, and the Term Definition macro eventually displayed a license-expired error after a long loading time. Overall, the app has good potential and provides real value for teams maintaining shared terminology, but the UI overlays, validation feedback, performance, and macro reliability need further refinement for a smoother production experience.
Highly Recommended, I am using it regurlary for my use

Overall, the Glossary application provides a smooth, user-friendly, and reliable experience. I tested the main functionalities, including creating and managing glossary terms, adding definitions, searching and filtering terms, multilingual glossary settings, displaying terms through the List Macro, and adding a term directly from a Confluence page. The functionalities tested worked as expected, with terms and definitions being saved and displayed correctly. The Add Term from Confluence Page functionality was particularly useful, as it allows users to select a term directly from a Confluence page and add it to the Glossary without having to manually recreate the term. The List Macro also worked well, displaying the available glossary terms in an organized and easy-to-navigate format. Overall, the application is intuitive, functional, and well-integrated with Confluence, and the tested features provide a good user experience.

The search - and term highlighting - also ignores the abbreviations and synonyms - which kind of defeats the purpose of including them. I'd also like to see each term on its own page rather than combined within a single page - but this is probably a personal choice. I think this is a great start, and we are seriously considering running with it (the price point at our license level makes it a no-brainer) however I feel addressing the following issues would actually make this plugin perfect: 1. Improve the search to work within the term, abbreviations, synonyms and description. 2. The term auto highlighting needs to work with plurals (if I have a definition for "vehicle" then the word "vehicles" should be highlighted). 3. Option to place terms definitions on separate pages and use excerpts to auto-generate a page like the current one that contains all definitions for a letter. 4. Clicking on a term that is highlighted should take me to the page that defines the term. 5. Highlight synonyms and abbreviations too! 6. Show the definitions under the letters that are applicable to the abbreviations and synonyms. 7. A picky one this - but I would like the auto highlighting to have a white background and just underline the word. The above would make this a super useful plugin and I suspect increase sales dramatically. As it is I am contemplating my choice between this and the tutorials by Terrence Caldwell detailing a roll-your-own solution.

I had high hopes for this plugin but was disappointed. I think the real strengths of a glossary tool should be on the search side and that is where this plugin is weakest. Here is what I found in version 2.1 running on Confluence 5.5.2. ADDING TERMS * Adding via the glossary navigation bar is straightforward and works well. * You have to add (initialize) a letter before you can add a term to it. This is an unnecessary step for a user. * Adding a term from another page by selecting the term seems easy. This is exactly how I would expect it to feel. * Adding the first term for an uninitialized letter fails. It adds only the term, not the definition. FINDING TERMS * Labels are not hyperlinks, thus I found no real use for them. * Search finds only the term, not any words in the definition! This is a huge presumption that you know what you are looking for and you don't need any context help finding it. * Search box in the glossary nav area only works within the letter you have selected. Not cool. If you know the letter you need, you have already performed half of the searching. This should work globally across all letters (or have that option for sites that do not have thousands of terms). * Highlighting defined terms on a page is slow, has no progress meter, and the results are very hard to read. Once you find a term, however, the definition is easy to read. * Search is not integrated with Confluence search, so you can't find terms from a non-glossary page. The irony is that Confluence finds definition words but not terms -- opposite of what the Glossary Search does.

Smart Terms Glossary [4.2*].review: This is a great glossary-type app. I've been involved in migrating the app from Data Center to Cloud, and the creativas team has been great at working around Atlassian's Cloud restrictions on HTML manipulation. You can use a browser extension (Chrome/Edge) or special preview mode to get the highlighting. While Cloud has Atlassian's new highlighting features (Rovo/Atlassian AI), those don't have any way to manage terms at the space or site level or embed them using macros. We also have a very large instance, and the whole creativas team met with us to solve some issues so that things like picking a term space are very fast at scale.

This is a great tool that provides much needed functionality to ensure that common or important terms or phrases have a single definition that does not require edits to multiple places. It requires a browser extension and while those extensions are not for every browser, they have them for some of the most common ones (Chrome, Safari, and Edge). Besides the functionality, the ability to make connections between related word, such as acronyms (or any other connection that you want to establish), is tremendously helpful. What this app is really missing, and not sure how this can be done, is to prevent a term from showing up when the context does not work for it. For example, Task Work Orders (TWO) and the #2 will create issues unless you term Task Work Order and use TWO as an acronym. Other example include "Security". If the reference is for data security rather than physical security (or some other variation), the context can be confusing. Even with some minor limitations, this app has solved a lot of problems for our content and removed the need to have terms defined in multiple places and minimized our need to use excerpt and excerpt include macros. By the way, the team behind this app is incredibly supportive and helpful. We have Smart Courses too and the people who own and operate this company have basically done everything possible to help us out, added new features when we asked for them (within a reasonable timeframe - not everything needs to be immediate), have troubleshooted any issue we have brought to their attention, and ALWAYS fixes whatever issues there are really quickly. I highly recommend this company and their products - they put a lot of care, consideration, and love into them.

Smart Terms is a great tool that helps you provide users with additional information on any Confluence page and you're very free in regards to what you put into the definition of any word / phrase. It is also very easy to disable the highlighting for a page if you have pages that shouldn't have words from the glossary highlighted. A big bonus to mention here is the great support from the vendor. We have always had our issues resolved very soon after raising them and bugs are fixed incredibly fast after submitting.

This app is great. It seems to do almost everything I want it to. It feels polished and reliable, which is what you need if you are going to invest a lot of time creating a glossary in Confluence using the app. The only thing it doesn't support is multiple definitions of the same term. Support is very good.
Good, prompt support from the team. Chrome was (and still kind of is) causing me issues with the extenstion though
Quick support and great concept. Would be even better if it offered direct API-Access for other terminology management software. :)

I decided to try the plugin in my company based on recommendations of a team member who used to use this app in his previous company. There were some problems with labeling terms and a small feature request on related vocabulary in the trial install. Both were quickly processed by the team, thanks to Hichem and Firas. Public release of the glossary will take place in nearest future, but all users from a test group were highly satisfied with the tool.

Intuitive Product and Responsive Support/Dev Teams I'm new to Confluence and all things Atlassian. I quickly found that I needed a glossary for my work and that built-in Confluence functionality wasn't going to be sufficient. Smart Terms came up repeatedly in my searches, so we gave it a try. Though not perfect it's really, really great for managing terms. The ability to define terms (including related terms) and display global highlighting has improved on the way I write technical documents and given me the flexibility to define-as-I-go or simply create an entry and define it later. Smart Terms has become critical to how I work in Confluence to the point that I don't know how I'd work without it. In the last paragraph I mentioned that Smart Terms wasn't perfect (but very close). During my product trial (before paying for anything, keep in mind) I found what I thought was undesirable behavior in how compound terms were highlighted. After some trial and error I was able to describe what was happening and what exactly I wanted. I submitted a case to Creativas Support. Within a day I had a response back that the dev team was able to reproduce my issue and they were actively working on a fix. Less than two weeks after first contact, they reported that the issue had been fixed. Thanks to Khawala and the dev team for such a refreshingly pleasant and prompt handling of the issue. I'm looking forward to seeing what more they can deliver with the product, but from my vantage point I think they earned all 4 stars.

Installed the app based on recommendations online and the Atlassian Staff Pick. Our company operates in a complex industry, and we are growing our team. Need this capability to ensure we can onboard new staff and keep consistent understanding across our groups. Trial install had some problems (scroll bar panes, label feature), but the support team clearly worked with Creativas' engineers to get a fix prioritized. Since then, our guys have given it good feedback, and looks like we'll get great use out of the glossary. Thanks to Khawla and Firas.

We are currently testing the tool and overall it is very positive. However, we are often asked by the users if it is possible to order the terms list based on the acronyms instead of the long versions of the terms. Usually users built their own lists also based on acronyms. We didn't find any possibility to switch this. Is it possible somehow, or can this be implemented with a simple "Sort by ..." button in the terms list?

Smart Terms is for me a perfect plug-in. The functionality is great and helps me and others to really come to terms with the vocabulary in use. With the new features added recently I had some questions and was very positively surprised of their support and how they helped and assisted. Great Product and great support.

Outstanding customer support! We really love the product and the people behind it. The Customer Success team went out of his way to help us with questions and support and it all worked out in the end. Thank you very much for this experience!
Very satisfied with the customer support! Quick with their response, going extra mile to understand the clients issue and solve it asap. Recommended!

Nice and handy app for glossary management. The bigger your company is, the greater use of this app is. In my opinion, access to it should be embed into newcomers onboarding process. The only downside is the not so intuitive installation, but this should not be an issue on a corporate level.

Good basic app for terminology management. Term highlighting is a nice feature. Easy enough to use and set up (at least for Confluence Cloud). It's a well-regarded app across our organisation and many people can't envision getting rid of it. The ability to create relationships between terms to create taxonomical structures would make this really powerful.
4 stars, great add-on, great support, A+++++++!

We tried to use a glossary for cloud version. Google chrome and firefox extensions seems to be not recogbized as installed in our browsers. Trying to click on "glossary" button results in "install an extension" even if it's already installed. Secondly, after installing an extension terms are highlighted but definitions are not displayed by hovering or clicking on terms in document's text. Server version seems to work as expected. So my opinion: 1. It's a mature enough extension for server (or maybe dc) version 2. For cloud version seems to be more efficient to look up for another solution. 3. Pricing for cloud and server are reasonable for light installations. For large ones maybe should consider splitting instances (for example if don't have an urge to support glossaries for everyone).

This is a very nice app, we tried it out and liked it quite a lot. However your pricing policy doesn't make any sense. We have around a hundred people on confluence, and correspondingly we would have to pay around $220 a month - a sum which no software should ever cost, the least of all a confluence addon. We are not gonna use your product going forward. Please, let us know when you change the pricing to something more reasonable. Thanks

UPD. It's not working! Should all my colleagues install the extension in a browser? Seriously? And what you say about Confluence Mobile App? Safari browser support? And where in your documentation says about the extension requirement? I want to use this add-on without a Google extension.

3 stars due to it being the best glossary app on the marketplace. However, it leaves a lot wanting. There is no option to highlight terms within other terms, rendering it useless for our data dictionary (which was the intended usage). Referencing existing terms within other terms is a must-have for any glossary. Other simple features such as CTRL+S to save and mass updates to terms (e.g. add a label to multiple terms) are missing as well.
great addon, wish chinese could be supported
Simple and easy to use glossary, makes it so much easier to define company-wide abbreviations and promoting the wording to the public

Nice features - such as defining certain areas (page titles, headings etc.) that you want to exclude from highlighting. As far as I can tell they have fantastic staff as well. Definitely a recommendation!

I can't say enough good things about this plugin! Smart Terms has been a godsend in helping us catalog the terms for our department's data dictionary. When an issue arose where our imports weren't working properly, the support we received from the TechUp team was second to none and they were with us every step of the way in debugging the issue. I applaud Kevin and the TechUp team for all of their hard work and appreciate all their help in keeping terms a top notch product!

I tested the plugin. Compared with other Glossary Plugins there are no errors. This plugin is implemented in a smooth way. It is used native Confluence objects. If you have a feature request, SW Vendor will consider it and provide you the next release very fast. Cooperation with SW Vendor is very good :)

Good plugin, using it extensively, but a couple of things would make it even better: * Can't use sub-script or super-script (everything else exists - bold, italics, underline etc) * No dedicated "Related to". I use "Other" as the classification, but would be good to get that. * No dedicated "Reference Page" where the term might be defined - again almost all of my terms have that added in the link manually, but sometimes I forget. If this was one of the attributes of a term that would be good too. The additions above would make this superb as a plugin.

Very intuitive to use Terminology Definition, and I like the feature-rich Pop-Ups in the content which do not influence the storage format of pages itself. PDF files from external sources seem not to work, we get a "Failed to Load PDF document" when including this file in our Terminology: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf The Elephant in the room: What I'm missing in this addon is functionality for using this within End-User Documentation (PDF and HTML): > Support for PDF Exports - I see no way to get Terms into a printable format at the end of an exported document. Is there a way to refer or include the terminology page someplace else without manually having to export my terms and "Layout" them in myself? > How about support for Translations, maybe Versioning of Glossary entries? On both points I'd suggest getting in contact with K15t and their "Scroll" series, because their Addon is missing a good glossary solution but otherwise has everything else for Content Publishing. Having Smart Terms functionality their Live-Viewport HTML view and PDF exports would be amazing.

Such a great plugin! We've deployed Smart Terms on a large instance (2000+ wikis) supporting over 26k users who have a multitude of terms/acronyms to navigate while trying to complete their work. Not only does this allow us to provide helpful information for our new employees, but also many of our experienced employees who may be on a cross-functional team/project. The quick response and support from Kevin/TechUp had been amazing, they really value and respond to feedback, and even implemented a suggestion that I had (only highlight first matching term) within a few days!
Very cool and funny glossary. Very simple to use!
For me the best glossary plugin on the whole marketplace. Very fast Support!

Glossary - Terminology Manager [3.6*].review: testing for migration to the Cloud ... seems like full of bugs !

Blocker: No Firefox Plugin. Very basic administration in the cloud version. It is not the same as seen in the video! Missing: - No filtering by tags - Search does not find anything contained in the description Anything else is as imagined. Seems to be fast.
Too many bugs. Really a pity - good simple design...

Demo video is misleading - interaction is absolutely not the same for Cloud as shown in video. When I deleted the term that was used on the page, than reloaded page, than clicked the A icon to highlight terms, the page stopped loading (error 1AMXKE5).

Seems to be a large discrepancy in feature set between the cloud and server versions when it comes to settings and management. There is no duplicate term detection so it is possible to create several duplicates. There is no term highlighting in the cloud version so it isn't clear what is a defined term and what isn't. Will continue testing but so far, not as useful of a test for another server instance as I had hoped.

After having used other options as glossary, we finally implemented this one and we don't regret it - very well customizable with the option to have *one* glossary in the whole confluence-instance, a superior support and a thought-through concept. A must-have addon!

Really nice tool, with some space to improve. Term status ("Approved", "Proposed") is not being tracked and there is no way to track who and when approved it. So it is just a text label, but this is a minor issue. Support is at superior level.

Don't look any further, you've found the perfect Glossary app for Confluence! After using another glossary app for several years which lacked key features and the vendor making promises they couldn't keep, we started looking for a proper alternative. Which we found in W Knowledge's Glossary app. Though the basic idea was already very good, we asked for some improvements and also found some bugs while trialing the app. The vendor responded instantly and was always helpful. Bugfixes and feature requests were implemented very fast, sometimes within days. The app is, from our point of view, now at an enterprise level in both reliability, features and support. Thanks Jennifer and team! Keep it up!

Finally a great and useful Glossary. I appreciate that is smoothly integrated with Confluence features and also the highlight mechanism. Singular/plural, synonyms, abbreviation or other forms are all highlighted, that’s awesome! Quick and accurate support! Appreciated!

I really like how this is coming along. There are some small bugs still (cant "unhighlight"; marking text with mouse still shows view.action tooltip; creating page with same name dialog doesnt close). But this works exactly like i would imagine a glossary in confluence. Language functions are good (improvement: same term title in different languages). i will watch out for this!

Glossary for Confluence Cloud [3.6*].review: An application that simply displays a glossary as wikipedia does with such a per-user fee is grossly overpriced. First, it should be a feature of Confluence itself... But well, with 100 users, it's $1500/year for a simple glossary. A pure joke. And for that price : - you must tell all your users to install a chrome extension to see the highlights (sorry people who use firefox or safari) - the software can't handle the accents, so for a word with two accents like "dÃ©jÃ ", you must add synonyms like "deja", "dÃ©ja" and "dejÃ " for this plugin to handle it - It doesn't handle acronyms either! If you create IT for "Information Technology" for example, it will highlight "it" in any sentence like "It is cool!" (but it's not) The plugin itself works well but that's not the problem. It's far too expensive for so few features. At this price, it should put a coffee on my desk every morning.
Fantastic app. Very intuitive and well integrated. An invaluable addition for our team.

Easy add-on to set up and use. The developer has very quick response time for any questions asked and outstanding support for a minor issue we had. Highly recommend this if a glossary of terms is needed for your team(s). Randy
